name: large-crossparadigm-comparison
title: Three substrates on the large Sego model (behavior-metric distances)
question: On the LARGE Sego 2022 blueprint (120x120, ~225-cell epithelium), how far does each mechanical substrate's emergent MOVEMENT and INTERACTION pattern sit from the CPM reference, measured by the cross-paradigm behavior metrics (per-cell displacement, MSD, neighbour-graph churn, infection-front speed, cell sorting)? Each metric is a DISTANCE from the CPM; the same-backend seed-to-seed distance is the null floor a match must approach.
experiment: Run sego_crossparadigm_large on CPM, vertex and center-based over rules-seeds {0,1,2} (N=60, 254 cells). For each behavior metric, score the cross-backend distance from the CPM (all seed combos) against the CPM-self seed-pair null floor. Script: scripts/compare_large_crossparadigm.py (results.json).
result: N=60, 254 cells, seeds 0-2. Distances as mean [cross/null x]: per-cell displacement -- null 3.77, VERTEX 2.93 (0.8x: within seed noise of the CPM), MUNK 8.52 (2.3x). MSD -- null 3.25, VERTEX 8.89 (2.7x: under-fluctuates), MUNK 75.4 (23x: over-mobile). neighbour-graph -- null 0.41, VERTEX 0.45 (1.1x), MUNK 0.48 (1.2x): both near the CPM's contact-churn. front-speed -- null 1.54, VERTEX 3.59 (2.3x), MUNK 7.37 (4.8x). sorting -- null 0.014, VERTEX 0.123 (8.5x: sorts differently -- its biggest gap), MUNK 0.021 (1.4x: near CPM). Each substrate matches a DIFFERENT facet of the CPM.

purpose.question: Now that center-based (munk) cells move and interact and the tissue is large enough for real spatial dynamics, which substrate reproduces the CPM's interaction pattern, and on which axes does each diverge?
purpose.mechanism: All three backends run the SAME shared mechanism (fields, rules, immune ODE) on the SAME large blueprint; only the mechanics node differs. Differences in the behavior metrics are therefore attributable to the substrate (CPM Metropolis lattice vs vertex confluent polygons vs center-based discs), not the biology.
purpose.expected_outcome: Vertex sits closest to the CPM on most axes but under-fluctuates (the capped- motility gap handed to vertex-cpm-fluctuation-match); center-based now MOVES (validating the munk fix) but, being uncalibrated, diverges most on displacement / MSD. The study reports the honest distances, not a forced agreement.

key_assumptions: The CPM is the reference substrate; vertex and munk are scored as distance-to-CPM on the shared large blueprint, same seeds.
Behavior metrics (compare/metrics.py) are the minimization target; the same-backend (seed-varied) distance is the matched null floor each cross distance is judged against.
Nothing is tuned here to force agreement — the study characterizes the substrates as they stand after the munk fix; calibration lives in adhesion-calibration / vertex-cpm-fluctuation-match.

behavior_tests.name: munk-moves-and-interacts
behavior_tests.description: Center-based cells now MOVE and change contacts — the munk per-cell displacement distance is well above a frozen baseline (validates the munk fix in this large regime).

behavior_tests.name: vertex-closest-to-cpm
behavior_tests.description: Vertex sits closer to the CPM than center-based on the motility axes (displacement + MSD distance).

pass_if.note: vertex_vs_cpm < munk_vs_cpm on displacement and MSD

behavior_tests.name: distances-above-null-floor
behavior_tests.description: Each cross-backend distance is reported against the CPM-self (seed-varied) null floor, so a genuine substrate difference is distinguished from seed noise.

pass_if.note: cross vs null floor reported per metric

controls.name: cpm-self-null
controls.description: CPM-vs-CPM (seed-varied) distance per metric — the matched null floor; a vertex/munk match must approach this, not 0.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The substrates already agree on movement/interaction (differences are seed noise).
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: The CPM-self null floor is reported alongside every cross distance; cross distances that exceed the null are real substrate differences.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Center-based still doesn't move (the fix didn't take at scale).
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: The munk displacement/MSD distances are well above the frozen baseline on the 225-cell tissue (munk-moves-and-interacts test).

limitations: N=60 steps, 3 seeds — a characterization run, not a long-horizon or high-replication study.
The behavior metrics are necessary but not sufficient for full pattern identity; visual (flipbook) agreement is a secondary check.
munk force parameters (jitter / adhesion-scale / chemotaxis-gain) are principled but uncalibrated; their values are pinned by adhesion-calibration, not here.
falsifiability: If the cross-backend distances were indistinguishable from the CPM-self null on every metric, the substrates would be behaviorally equivalent on the large model and no calibration would be warranted. The reported distances overturn that.

report.title: How far each substrate's movement/interaction pattern sits from the CPM (large Sego)
report.verdict: Three-way behavior-metric comparison on the large Sego model (N=60, 254 cells, seeds 0-2). No substrate matches the CPM on every axis; each diverges on specific ones, giving concrete calibration targets. VERTEX is closest on per-cell trajectory (displacement 2.93, BELOW the CPM-self null 3.77 -- within seed noise) and contact churn (0.445 vs null 0.414), but UNDER-FLUCTUATES (MSD 2.7x null -- the capped- motility ceiling handed to vertex-cpm-fluctuation-match) and SORTS cells differently (sorting 8.5x null -- its largest gap). CENTER-BASED (munk) now MOVES and interacts (displacement 8.52, MSD 75.4 -- validating the munk fix; it was frozen before), with contact topology (0.482) and sorting (0.021) CLOSE to the CPM, but is OVER-mobile (MSD 23x null) and diverges most on infection-front speed (4.8x null) -- uncalibrated.
report.objective: Quantify, with the new behavior metrics, the distance-to-CPM of the vertex and center-based substrates' emergent movement and interaction patterns on the large Sego blueprint, against the CPM-self null floor.
report.main_insight: Each substrate reproduces a DIFFERENT facet of the CPM: vertex matches per-cell trajectories and contact churn but under-fluctuates and mis-sorts; center-based (now unfrozen) matches contact topology and sorting but over-moves. The behavior metrics localize exactly which axis each substrate needs calibrated on.
report.caveat: N=60, 3 seeds; munk parameters uncalibrated; metrics are a necessary-not-sufficient proxy for full pattern identity.

study_card.goal: Measure how close vertex and center-based get to the CPM's movement/interaction pattern on the large Sego model, as distance-to-CPM behavior metrics.
study_card.mechanism: Same shared mechanism + same large blueprint on all three substrates; only the mechanics node differs, so behavior-metric distances isolate the substrate effect.
study_card.why_before_next: Establishes the quantitative baseline the calibration studies (adhesion-calibration, vertex-cpm-fluctuation-match) minimize against, on the large tissue.
study_card.expected_result: Vertex closest to CPM (but under-fluctuating); center-based moves but diverges most; all distances above the null floor.
study_card.main_expert_question: Which metric axis matters most as the headline distance-to-CPM target for calibration?

visualizations.name: Spatial playback — CPM on the large Sego tissue

config.title: Large Sego 2022 — CPM reference playback (120x120, ~225-cell epithelium)

biological_summary:
THE VIDEO (spatial-playback-cpm-large). The playback opens on a confluent ~225-cell epithelial sheet (H, uninfected) tiling the central 120x120 patch, with a small seed of infected cells (I) and a sparse set of recruited immune effectors (macrophages M, NK, CD8) at the margins. Over the 80-step run the frames show the canonical Sego 2022 flu-lung sequence play out across a tissue large enough for real spatial structure:

1. INFECTION FRONT. Infected cells (I) secrete the virus field, which diffuses into neighbouring sites; the H->I transition fires at rate g_hv*field['virus'], so infection advances as a roughly radial front eating into the H sheet from the seed outward. This is the geometry the `front_speed_distance` readout measures: the CPM front has a characteristic advance rate that the vertex (2.3x null) and munk (4.8x null) substrates spread faster than, because their mechanics move the virus-secreting cells differently.

2. DEATH + CLEARANCE. Behind the front, infected cells die (I->D, rate mu_i) both intrinsically and by NK/CD8 contact-kill (rate ~ shared_surface with the effector * resist / size). Dying cells (D) appear as a trailing shell inside the infected zone, and a slow D->H regeneration term lets a fraction of cleared sites return to the uninfected state. The visible outcome is a moving annulus: H ahead of the front, I at the front, D/clearing behind it.

3. IMMUNE INFILTRATION. Infected cells also secrete chemokine; recruited M/NK/CD8 migrate up that gradient into the lesion. In the CPM these effectors are the cells that actually MOVE through the sheet — the epithelium itself is near-static (Metropolis fluctuations about fixed lattice positions), so most of the per-cell displacement and MSD signal is immune-cell motility plus front remodelling, not bulk epithelial flow. This is why center-based (munk), which lets every disc drift, over-shoots MSD by 23x: it moves cells the CPM holds still.

WHAT THE METRICS READ OFF THIS VIDEO. `per_cell_displacement` / `msd` quantify how far cells travel (immune infiltration + front churn); `neighbour_graph` quantifies contact remodelling as H->I->D sweeps through and effectors dock onto targets (the CPM's contact-churn is matched to ~1.1-1.2x by both other substrates); `front_speed` quantifies the infection-front geometry above; `sorting_index` quantifies how sharply cell types segregate (H/I/D zoning + immune clustering) — the CPM keeps types well-mixed at the front, which is where vertex diverges most (8.5x null, it over-segregates). The video is the qualitative object; the readouts are its projection onto five scalar axes, each a distance a calibrated substrate must drive toward the CPM-self null floor.

SECONDARY CHECK. The video is a necessary-not-sufficient visual companion to the numbers: two substrates can match a scalar metric while looking different, so the playback is where a reviewer confirms the metrics are reading the pattern they intend. It is CPM-only by design — the reference the distances are measured from; the three-way side-by-side playback lives on flu-lung-crossparadigm (small tissue).
